introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. IN SECTIONS B AND C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen; answer any two questions). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae Booklets may be used.
enonce_intro_markdown: A woman has 1,500 FCFA only to buy $x$ cups of beans and $y$ cups of rice to prepare food for her house hold.

Modélisé en « 2 sur 3 » pour la Section B et « 2 sur 3 » pour la Section C ; la Section A n'a pas de règle (tout est obligatoire). Q5 (d) : la phrase « every member of the household has to consume 2/3 of a cup of beans and a cup of rice » est ambiguë. Lecture retenue : 2/3 de tasse du mélange haricots + riz par personne, objectif linéaire x + y (maximum entier 22 en x = 8, y = 14), donc 33 personnes. Lecture littérale (2/3 de tasse de haricots ET 1 tasse de riz par personne) : 12 personnes ; notée dans le corrigé.

Q5 (c) : tracé à faire par le candidat (papier millimétré, 2 cm pour 5 unités) : décrit dans le corrigé (droites, côtés à ombrer, sommets de la région O(0,0), A(7,5 ; 15), B(12 ; 6)). Aucune figure imprimée dans le sujet.
Q5 (a) : « house hold » dans le sujet (faute d'impression recopiée).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Given that a cup of beans costs 100 FCFA and a cup of rice costs 50 FCFA, show that $2x+y\le30$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cost of $x$ cups of beans is $100x$ FCFA and the cost of $y$ cups of rice is $50y$ FCFA. She has only $1\,500$ FCFA, so the total cost cannot exceed this amount:

$$100x+50y\le1\,500.$$

Dividing both sides by $50$:

$$2x+y\le30,\ \text{as required.}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Given that:

- the quantity of beans is at least half the quantity of rice
- the quantity of beans is at most twice the quantity of rice,

write down two inequalities in terms of $x$ and $y$ that satisfy the conditions in (b). *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- "Beans at least half the rice": $x\ge\dfrac12y$, which is $y\le2x$.
- "Beans at most twice the rice": $x\le2y$.

**The two inequalities are $y\le2x$ and $x\le2y$** (equivalently $x\ge\frac12y$ and $x\le2y$).

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) On a graph paper, taking 2 cm to represent 5 units on both axes shade, so as to leave unshaded, the region represented by these 3 inequalities. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three inequalities are $2x+y\le30$, $y\le2x$ and $x\le2y$ (with $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$ since quantities cannot be negative).

**Scale:** $2$ cm for $5$ units on both axes, so the axes run from $0$ to $15$ on the $x$-axis (6 cm) and from $0$ to $30$ on the $y$-axis (12 cm).

**Boundary lines** (draw them as solid lines, the inequalities are non-strict):

| Line | Two points to plot | Side to keep (unshaded) |
|---|---|---|
| $2x+y=30$ | $(0,30)$ and $(15,0)$ | below the line (test $(0,0)$: $0\le30$) |
| $y=2x$ | $(0,0)$ and $(10,20)$ | below the line, i.e. on the right (test $(5,0)$: $0\le10$) |
| $x=2y$, i.e. $y=\frac12x$ | $(0,0)$ and $(14,7)$ | above the line (test $(0,5)$: $0\le10$) |

**Shade the unwanted side of each line.** The region left unshaded is the triangle with vertices

- $O(0,0)$,
- $A(7.5,\,15)$: intersection of $y=2x$ and $2x+y=30$ (since $4x=30$),
- $B(12,\,6)$: intersection of $x=2y$ and $2x+y=30$ (since $5y=30$).

The unshaded region is the triangle $OAB$ (boundaries included).

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Given also that every member of the household has to consume $\dfrac23$ of a cup of beans and a cup of rice, find the maximum number of people this woman can feed after preparing the meal. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading used.** Each person consumes $\dfrac23$ of a cup of the beans-and-rice food. If $x+y$ cups are prepared, the number of people fed is

$$N=\frac{x+y}{2/3}=\frac32(x+y),$$

so we must maximise $x+y$ over the unshaded region (cups are whole numbers).

At the vertices of the region: $O$ gives $0$; $A(7.5,15)$ gives $x+y=22.5$; $B(12,6)$ gives $18$. The maximum of $x+y$ is near $A$, but $A$ is not a whole-number point.

Test the whole-number points near $A$ inside the region ($2x+y\le30$, $y\le2x$, $x\le2y$):

- $(7,15)$: $15\le14$ fails;
- $(8,15)$: $2(8)+15=31>30$ fails;
- $(8,14)$: $30\le30$, $14\le16$, $8\le28$ all hold, so $x+y=22$;
- $(7,14)$ gives only $21$, $(9,12)$ gives $21$.

The largest whole-number value is $x+y=22$, at $x=8$ cups of beans and $y=14$ cups of rice.

$$N=\frac32\times22=33.$$

(Even without the whole-number restriction, $x+y\le22.5$ gives $N\le33.75$, so at most $33$ people.)

**The woman can feed at most $33$ people.**

*Note.* If the sentence is read literally as "$\frac23$ cup of beans and $1$ cup of rice per person", the count is limited by $\frac32x$ (beans) and $y$ (rice); the best whole-number choice then is $x=9$, $y=12$, which feeds $12$ people. The first reading (a linear objective on the graph, as the question is set) is the one retained.
